look_here_first: Start with the long naked flower stalk and perfume. Fragrant gaillardia is a taprooted perennial with a basal rosette, very long mostly leafless peduncles, fragrant heads, and rays that may be tiny or completely absent, leaving a pincushion-like purple-brown disk.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: rays variable from present to nearly absent

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves mostly basal and spatulate to oblanceolate

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: dry limestone or sandy prairie habitat

lookalikes.differences: Unlike G. pulchella and G. amblyodon, the flowering stalks are much more scapose and rays may be absent. Unlike G. aestivalis, foliage is concentrated basally rather than distributed strongly along leafy stems.
